context_requirements: Functional sensory neurons or itch-competent neural tissue (dorsal root ganglion) for direct antipruritic mechanisms
Immune cells (mast cells, T cells, ILC2) and keratinocytes for cytokine-mediated antipruritic effects
An active itch/inflammatory signaling context (e.g., IL-13, IL-31, TSLP, histamine) to antagonize
None of the nine immortalized cancer cell lines provide these contexts
falsifiers: Reproducible, dose-dependent transcriptional changes in any of the nine cell lines at 6 h or 24 h that are specific to antipruritic drugs and not seen with vehicle
Shared gene-expression signature across multiple antipruritic drugs in these lines
Enrichment of itch, cytokine, or neuroactive signaling pathways among differentially expressed landmark genes

evidence.supports: IL-13 and anti-IL-13 antibody effects on itch are mediated through human dorsal root ganglion neurons, not through cancer cell lines
Cyclosporine A reduces itch via epidermal nerve density and itch-related receptor genes in dorsal root ganglion in a mouse atopic dermatitis model
Antipruritic effects of antifungals and dexamethasone were assessed in mouse contact dermatitis and keratinocytes, not in the nine cancer lines
Oxymatrine antipruritic mechanism involves immune and inflammatory pathways in itch models, not direct cancer cell line transcription
Yinqiao antipruritic formula acts through Th2 cytokine-cytokine receptor pathways in atopic dermatitis mice, requiring immune context absent from the panel
